title: US STOCKS-Wall St slips as Turkey's currency worries hurt bank stocks
text:
Shutterstock photo
* Nielsen jumps after activist investor pushes for sale
* Financials fall on concerns of a plummeting Turkish lira
* Apple and Amazon hit record highs
* Indexes down: Dow 0.40 pct, S&P 0.24 pct, Nasdaq 0.06 pct
* Graphic: World FX rates in 2018 https://reut.rs/2vFv6Ue (Changes comment, adds details, updates prices)
By Amy Caren Daniel
Aug 13 (Reuters) - U.S. stock indexes fell on Monday as aplummeting Turkish lira weighed on shares of big U.S. lenders,but losses on the Nasdaq were limited by high-flying companiessuch as Apple and Amazon that hit record highs.
The financials .SPSY slipped 0.63 percent as U.S. bankstocks, like its European counterparts, bore the brunt ofinvestor worries over exposure to Turkey's crisis.
Shares of CitigroupC.N , Bank of AmericaBAC.N , WellsFargo WFC.N and JP Morgan JPM.N were down between 0.7percent and 1 percent.
The lira TRY= has tumbled more than 40 percent https://reut.rs/2vFv6Ue against the dollar this year on worries over President TayyipErdogan's increasing control over the economy and deterioratingrelations with the United States. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nL5N1V407X
"While the Turkish lira does not pose a direct threat to theUnited States, it can temporarily impact sentiment and tip theinvestor to being risk-off," said Dave Donabedian, chiefinvestment officer of CIBC Private Wealth Management in Atlanta.
"Investors are buying technology as they are momentumstocks. Some of the large-cap tech stocks have a halo as strongearnings growers."
The technology sector .SPLRCT rose 0.18 percent and wasthe only S&P sector to be trading higher.
Apple's shares AAPL.O jumped as much as 1.6 percent to hita record high of $210.95 and Amazon.comAMZN.O rose as much as2.1 to an all-time high of $1,925, while Google-parent Alphabet GOOGL.O gained 0.2 percent.
At 12:38 a.m. EDT the Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI was down 101.99 points, or 0.40 percent, at 25,211.15, the S&P500 .SPX was down 6.94 points, or 0.24 percent, at 2,826.34and the Nasdaq Composite .IXIC was down 5.08 points, or 0.06percent, at 7,834.03.
Among stocks, Harley DavidsonHOG.N fell 4 percent afterPresident Donald Trump backed boycotting American motorcyclemanufacturer. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nL1N1V303F
Netflix's shares dipped 0.5 percent and was the only one ofthe FAANG stocks trading lower, after the video streamingservice provider said its Chief Financial Officer David Wellsplans to step down. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nL4N1V44RW
Nielsen HoldingsNLSN.N jumped 9.2 percent, the most onthe S&P 500, after activist investor Elliott Managementdisclosed a stake and said would push for a sale of theTV-ratings company. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nL4N1V44IW
VF CorpVFC.N dropped 3.9 percent after the apparel makerdecided to spin off Lee and Wrangler jeans into a separatepublic company. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nL4N1V43SU
Declining issues outnumbered advancers for a 2.33-to-1 ratioon the NYSE and for a 1.98-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.
The S&P index recorded 11 new 52-week highs and eight newlows, while the Nasdaq recorded 55 new highs and 90 new lows.
